name: The last events
note: Twenty events for the two classes the retired targets left materially short: twelve invasions chosen for what they became, eight sites chosen for what they teach. The counting stops here; density and silence rules bind from now on.

events.title: Toramana carries Huna rule deep into central India
events.evidence: The Eran boar inscription dated in his reign, and his coins across Malwa.
events.becomes: A Huna king using Sanskrit inscriptions and local administrative forms within a generation — the assimilation running faster than the war.

events.title: Mihirakula is broken at Sondani by an Indian coalition
events.evidence: Yashodharman's victory pillars at Sondani, boasting rule from the Brahmaputra to the western ocean.
events.becomes: The Huna threat ends as a political force; the coalition dissolves within a decade, and the pillar's empire never outlives its inscription.
events.note: The victory column outlasted the victory by fourteen centuries.

events.title: Koppam: the Chola and Chalukya armies bleed each other on the Krishna
events.evidence: Both dynasties' inscriptions claiming the day; a Chola king dies on the field and his brother is crowned on it.
events.becomes: A succession made on the battlefield — Rajendra II crowned amid the fighting — and a rivalry pushed one generation closer to exhaustion.

events.title: The Cholas sack Kalyani and carry off a door-guardian
events.evidence: The dvarapala taken to Darasuram, where it still stands, inscribed as loot from Kalyani.
events.becomes: A trophy with a label: the clearest surviving object of inter-imperial war in the medieval south.

events.title: Malik Kafur rides to Madurai and back
events.evidence: Amir Khusrau's campaign account, and the sudden appearance of southern temple gold in Delhi's treasury records.
events.becomes: No annexation — a demonstration: the south is reachable. Vijayanagara is founded within a generation by men who absorbed the lesson.

events.title: Raichur: Vijayanagara takes the doab with massed matchlocks
events.evidence: The Portuguese eyewitness account of Fernão Nunes, and the Bijapur chronicles' admission of the loss.
events.becomes: Krishnadevaraya at his zenith and gunpowder decisive in a Deccan field battle — the sultanates ally within a generation, and Talikota is the answer.

events.title: The Ahoms destroy Turbak's invasion and take his guns
events.evidence: The buranjis' detailed account, including the captured firearms reverse-engineered afterwards.
events.becomes: Ahom firearms manufacture begins from captured pieces — the frontier state arms itself with the invader's own technology.

events.title: Colachel: Travancore defeats a European power in pitched battle
events.evidence: The Dutch East India Company's own records of the defeat, and the captured commander De Lannoy's later service.
events.becomes: The Dutch never recover on the Malabar coast; their captured commander rebuilds Travancore's army on European lines for its own king.
events.note: The losing commander switched sides and spent thirty years building his captor's army. Both parties considered it a good bargain.

events.title: Kanhoji Angre's fleet makes the Konkan coast unsafe for Europe
events.evidence: Company and Portuguese records of captured ships and failed punitive expeditions across three decades.
events.becomes: Proof that European navies could be resisted in coastal waters — a proof that died with the Angre fleet in 1756, one year before Plassey.

events.title: The Seven Years' Devastation empties Manipur
events.evidence: The Manipuri chronicle's account of the Burmese occupation, and the refugee settlements in Cachar.
events.becomes: Manipur's depopulation and the Anglo-Burmese war's eastern casus belli — the valley re-founded under a British-aligned king.

events.title: Abdali sacks Delhi the year of Plassey
events.evidence: The Delhi chronicles of the sack, and the Company's simultaneous correspondence from Bengal.
events.becomes: The old empire is stripped in the same twelve months the new power takes Bengal's revenue — the succession happens at both ends at once.

events.title: Akbar takes Chittor and the memory outlives the war
events.evidence: The Akbarnama's own account of the massacre after the fall, and the fort's abandonment as a capital.
events.becomes: Mewar moves its capital to the hills and never submits fully; the siege enters Rajput memory beside 1303, and Udaipur is the consequence.

events.title: Sirkap: Taxila's second city, laid out on a Greek grid
events.evidence: Marshall's excavation of the gridded city with its stupas, temples and the double-headed eagle shrine.
events.note: A Greek plan filling up with Buddhist shrines — the whole northwest in one street plan.

events.title: The Chudamani Vihara: Srivijaya builds a monastery at Nagapattinam
events.evidence: The larger Leiden copper plates recording the Srivijayan king's endowment and Rajaraja's grant of a village to it.
events.note: The empire the Cholas would raid in 1025 was funding a monastery in the Chola port in 1006. Trade, faith and war shared one sea.

events.title: Bhitari: the pillar where the Gupta-Huna war is narrated
events.evidence: Skandagupta's Bhitari pillar inscription describing the war, the shaken throne and the restoration.

events.title: Badami's cave temples are cut into the sandstone gorge
events.evidence: Cave 3's dedicatory inscription of Mangalesha, dated by regnal year — the earliest dated Chalukya monument.

events.title: Kaveripattinam declines as the sea and the river both withdraw
events.evidence: The abandonment horizon in the excavated wharf area, and the Manimekalai's memory of a city taken by the sea.

events.title: Bhinmal: where Brahmagupta computed, a market city of the west
events.evidence: Xuanzang's description of Pi-lo-mo-lo, and the Brahmasphutasiddhanta's own colophon placing its author there.

events.title: Lakhamandal and the Yamuna valley's stone temples
events.evidence: The temple complex and its inscription naming a queen's endowment.

events.title: Udayagiri: the Gupta caves where kingship and cosmology are carved together
events.evidence: Cave 5's Varaha panel with Chandragupta II's inscribed date — the boar raising the earth as the king watches.
events.note: A political statement in mythological grammar, dated to the year.
